evidence: Workbook #20: 'The reference is a committed, static baseline - not regenerated, fetched, or nondeterministic on any pinned value.' Skill quality-checks.md ### 20: same rows every seed run, no random ids, no wall-clock-derived values, no boot-time fetch moving a graded figure, fixed clock is the only time source graded rules use. (1) Committed static baseline: solution/app is plain committed source; solve.sh only refuses install while the DB is open, then 'cp -a "$(dirname "$0")/app/." /app/' and 'rm -f -- "$database_path" ...-wal ...-shm' - no generation, download or build step. Frozen hashes recomputed (sha256sum) for src/bootstrap.js 7ea92a2c..., src/db.js 0367a73b..., src/index.js 708f94cb..., public/js/app.js a8dbefe3..., board.js a177dc0c..., threads.js 5bc5a384..., solve.sh 1df2ed04..., seed_data.json a1c65c80... - all equal the matching_source_files in raw-evidence-index.json. (2) Seed: solution/app/src/seed_data.json is byte-identical to environment/assets/seed_data.json (cmp, both a1c65c80...); db.js reads it from __dirname (line ~10 of db.js: path.join(__dirname,'seed_data.json')), no network. seedIfEmpty runs only when users is empty; inserts users/jobs/applications with seed ids (JOB-PLAT/JOB-DATA/JOB-DSGN, APP-101...), a fixed application created_at '2026-06-15T09:00:00Z', messages/notes with seed created_at in seed order (AUTOINCREMENT ids therefore deterministic), and read markers mapped deterministically from read_count to those ids. Fixed password from the brief. No random or wall-clock value enters any seeded row; restarts never reseed. (3) No boot-time fetch: no outbound http(s) URL in solution app sources; client fetch() is same-origin to its own API only. bootstrap.js answers /api/health and proxies to a worker on 127.0.0.1. (4) Runtime nondeterminism is confined to non-pinned values: index.js:59 now()=new Date().toISOString() stamps sessions/activity/actions/notes/messages/new applications; index.js:60 uid() = crypto.randomBytes(3) for new JOB-/APP- ids; index.js:88 random session tokens. Every graded ordering uses integer ids or positions (activity ORDER BY a.id DESC line 189, messages ORDER BY id 407-412, columns ORDER BY position,id line 199, unread/seen via message ids). Candidate list ORDER BY created_at,id (line 173) puts seeded rows (fixed 2026-06-15) before new ones under any realistic clock, and criterion K only says the list 'includes' specific applications. Wall-clock times are only displayed (app.js:21 when(), shown in activity/notes/messages) and no criterion, prompt or app_context grades a timestamp, date or created id (grep of tests/scored/*, tests/gates/*, app_context.md for timestamp|date|clock|UTC|APP-|JOB- found none). The brief/notes state no fixed clock and no graded rule is time-based, so 'fixed clock is the only time source graded rules use' holds vacuously. Random 6-hex app/job ids cannot collide with 3-digit seeded ids; collision among new ids is ~1e-5 per run. (5) Dependencies: package.json pins express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1 exactly; both images install the same exact versions globally (environment/Dockerfile identical to template; tests/Dockerfile). Transitive resolution happens at image build, which is template-controlled, not a reference regeneration. Colderwater lessons check: lesson 15 restart durability - seedIfEmpty never reseeds a populated DB, so restart re-reads are deterministic; lesson 19 scripted golden harness - raw-evidence-index cites a scripted golden run on these exact solution bytes (hashes verified), though that is not a configured judge run or Oracle grade and is not needed to decide this source-level row. No other lesson pattern bears on row 20. Adversarial: a broken reference that regenerated seed rows with random ids or wall-clock timestamps would be caught here, but this reference does not; a conforming alternative is not affected because row 20 concerns only the reference.
